title: Evolution plane — promote the background worker to the primary path, and make forgetting a real algorithm
description:
Fifth of seven plane epics (see `project-management/design/ADVANCED_MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `project-management/AI_NATIVE_AGILE.md`).

**Invariant this plane owns:** every derived record links to its sources — no orphans.

**A. The architecture already has the right idea filed under the wrong priority.** `Consolidator` runs synchronously on the write path with a `consolidate_every_n` throttle, and `scripts/consolidate_pending.py` exists as what the README calls an 'async/background worker escape hatch'. The research says the escape hatch is the main road. Sleep-time compute formalises it: when an agent is idle but still holds the context, it should be reasoning about that context offline — anticipating likely queries and precomputing derived quantities, turning raw context into learned context so that test-time compute drops. Every expensive operation in this plane (reflection, entity resolution, community summarisation, decay sweeps, reindexing) is a background job, and none of them belongs on a user-facing write. The synchronous consolidator stays, but as the read-your-writes special case rather than the default.

What that requires is unglamorous and specific: a durable `memory_jobs` table with claim semantics that survive a worker dying mid-job. `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is the standard shape, and whether Db2 12.1.5 supports it with the semantics we need is spiked rather than assumed (EVOL-2) — this repo has already been bitten twice by Db2 dialect gaps (vectors not parameter-bindable per the EPIC-25 audit; `VECTOR_SERIALIZE` not combinable with `VECTOR_DISTANCE` in one statement per the ORC-2 workaround), so assuming ANSI-standard behaviour here would be the third time.

**B. Nothing currently forgets, and unbounded growth is the number one production failure mode for memory systems.** TTL and `purge_expired()` handle explicit expiry, which covers a small fraction of what should decay. The psychology has a better-tested answer than any heuristic we would invent: the DSR model (Difficulty, Stability, Retrievability) as implemented in FSRS, which replaced Ebbinghaus's exponential with a *power law* in v4 because it fit real review logs measurably better. The reason that matters here is mechanical rather than aesthetic — a power law has a falling hazard rate, so a memory that has already survived a long interval becomes progressively more durable, which is exactly the behaviour wanted for a fact that keeps being retrieved across sessions. Retrieval raises stability (the spacing effect); disuse lowers retrievability.

Decay must never hard-delete. The ladder is hot (indexed, full fidelity) -> warm (indexed, summary only, original archived) -> cold (archived, not indexed, restorable) -> purged (tombstone plus audit record). And the audit trail must keep three causes distinguishable: user-initiated `forget()`, AI-initiated reconciliation, and system-initiated decay. The SDK already draws the first two apart — that discipline extends to the third rather than being diluted by it.

**C. Two write paths the SDK doesn't have.** *Reflection*: periodically take the recent high-importance records, ask the model for the salient higher-level inferences, and write those back as first-class retrievable records with `DERIVED_FROM` edges — triggered on cumulative importance crossing a threshold, not on a timer, so quiet periods cost nothing. *Evolution* (A-MEM): a new record updates the tags, context, and links of its existing neighbours, so the network refines itself instead of only accreting.

**D. Procedural memory currently stores text, and the research says it should store verified, executable, statistically-tracked routines.** Agent Workflow Memory reports +24.6% (Mind2Web) and +51.1% (WebArena) relative success from inducing reusable workflows out of successful trajectories; Voyager's skill library shows the same pattern with a success-gated write. The design consequence is that `procedural` becomes the one memory type with a closed feedback loop — written only on verified success, carrying a success rate updated on each reuse — and therefore the one place a reinforcement signal can legitimately enter the store.

**The uncomfortable spike that gates half this epic:** a controlled ablation (*Verbatim Chunks Beat Extracted Artifacts*, arXiv:2601.00821) found raw conversation chunks outperforming LLM-extracted facts for long-conversation memory. Consolidation is neither free nor obviously net-positive, and this repo already has the harness to settle it (`benchmarks/quality/longmemeval_adapter.py`, `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/consolidator.py`). EVOL-6 runs that ablation, and EVOL-3/EVOL-7 do not ship if it loses.

**Depends on:** EPIC-27 STOR-1 (reflection and evolution both write edges). EVOL-4/EVOL-5 depend on EPIC-29 RTRV-6 for access statistics. **Blocks:** nothing downstream.
